examples.text: Démarquer du linge.
Démarquer dans un livre l’endroit où le lecteur s’est arrêté.

Angèle. — … Ribadier, Robineau… Même initiale… pas besoin de faire démarquer mon linge ni mon argenterie !
Thommereux, se levant. — C’est ça… un mariage d’économie ! Je connaissais le mariage d’amour, le mariage de raison, mais ce mariage-là, non !… Qu’on épouse un homme parce qu’il a de jolies moustaches, ou qu’il porte bien la toilette, je le comprends encore… Mais que ce soit pour ne pas démarquer son linge ! Ah ! Non ! Ça me dépasse !

glosses: Enlever sa marque à une marchandise, enlever l’étiquette attestant son origine, afin de la vendre au rabais, ou pour s’en débarrasser, si c’est le produit d’un vol.

examples.text: Il fut convaincu d’avoir démarqué toute l’argenterie.

glosses: Démarquer le stock d’invendus : réduire le prix des marchandises pour les écouler plus vite.
Démarquer un ouvrage savant : recopier une partie du contenu, sans discernement, en espérant s’attribuer le mérite d’une connaissance approfondie du sujet.

examples.text: D’autres encore, comme Marisol Touraine ou Manuel Valls, démarquent carrément la typographie des affiches d’En marche !.

glosses: Démarquer un roman, une œuvre d’imagination : Plagier, copier sans scrupule une œuvre qui fait recette, dans son concept, ou mot pour mot, dans des passages isolés.

examples.text: Démarquer un écrit peu connu ; démarquer un article d’encyclopédie spécialisée.

glosses: Être la copie, la reproduction de quelque chose.

examples.text: Avant de le rencontrer, j’ignorais que la physionomie d’un vivant pût exprimer tant de haine, de désespoir, et démarquer à ce point les faces damnées de ceux qui tombèrent « dans l’endroit du lac le plus profond ».

glosses: Retrancher les points qu’on a marqués.

examples.text:
— Monsieur, lui dis-je pendant qu’il me donnait des cartes, auriez-vous la complaisance de démarquer ?
Il fit passer assez précipitamment ses jetons de gauche à droite.

glosses: To reduce the price of.

To subtract marks or points from, for an error.

examples.text: The writing is good, but I had to mark you down for failing to cite references.

glosses: To write down.

examples.text: They could not take what he'd become / and mark him down as free, / and so they trapped him with his dream / and nailed him to a tree.

glosses: To bring down the size, quantity, quality, value or intensity of something; to diminish, to lower.

examples.text: to reduce weight, speed, heat, expenses, price, personnel etc.

Becoming more aware of the progress that scientists have made on behavioral fronts can reduce the risk that other natural scientists will resort to mystical agential accounts when they exceed the limits of their own disciplinary training.
Most train operators have reduced services with emergency timetables, as they struggle to cope with a rapid increase in staff absences due to the Omicron variant of COVID.

glosses: To lose weight.
To bring to an inferior rank; to degrade, to demote.

examples.text: to reduce a sergeant to the ranks
My father, the eldest son of an ancient but reduced family, left me with little.
nothing so excellent but a man may falten upon something or other belonging to it whereby to reduce it .
Having reduced their foe to misery beneath their fears.
Hester Prynne was shocked at the condition to which she found the clergyman reduced.

glosses: To humble; to conquer; to subdue; to capture.

examples.text: to reduce a province or a fort

glosses: To bring to an inferior state or condition.

examples.text: to reduce a city to ashes

glosses: To be forced by circumstances (into something one considers unworthy).

The press release calls him "the hottest female impressionist in show business today." (One wonders how many more words press agents will have to come up with before they are reduced to actually saying "drag queen.")

glosses: To decrease the liquid content of (a food) by boiling much of its water off.

examples.text: Serve the oxtails with mustard or a sauce made by reducing the soup, if any is left, to a slightly thick sauce.

glosses: To add electrons / hydrogen or to remove oxygen.

examples.text: Formaldehyde can be reduced to form methanol.

glosses: To produce metal from ore by removing nonmetallic elements in a smelter.

examples.text: It is important that all business contracts be reduced to writing.

examples.text: The first vowel of support is reduced to schwa by most English speakers.

glosses: The result of copying; an identical or nearly identical duplicate of an original.

examples.text: Please bring me at least 200 copies of this report. The photocopier is down the hall on the right.

His new book is out. I have a signed copy. He'll send you a copy if you want one. He's giving free copies to his former colleagues who want one. The press run is 3000 copies, and he hopes to sell more press runs after this one.
I already saw their draft. She emailed me a copy yesterday. I can forward it to you so that you have your own copy.
I have not the vanity to think my copy equal to the original.

glosses: The result of copying; an identical or nearly identical duplicate of an original.

examples.text: Every cell in this organism contains a copy of each gene, but whether that copy will be expressed depends on complex factors of cell differentiation and epigenetics.

examples.text: That handbag is a copy. You can tell because the buckle is different.

glosses: To give or transmit a copy to (a person).

examples.text: Make sure you copy me on that important memo.

glosses: To place a copy of an object in memory for later use.
